summary: Leaders at sea and in the air: the rank ladder inlined in the four modifier passes, the spread's floor, the friendly fire's leader, the targeting static, the disengage truncation and the two targeting technology keys.

addresses.name: CNavalCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CNavalCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers(CNavalCombatant* this, CCombatant* other, int flag)
addresses.comment: Slot 19 for a naval fight: per fleet and per ship, each modifier put on the ship (CSubUnit::AddCombatModifier). Poor screens (defence only), the submarines' surprise (attack only), difficulty, the ship's own experience with its pride bonus, mission efficiency, dissent, lack of supplies, wind and rain (attack only), the night (attack only, by the side's own adjuster) and the leader. **The surprise is rolled in the first round only** - an attacking fleet with a submarine, `Random() % 100 < NAVAL_COMBAT_SUB_SURPRISE_CHANCE` - and then holds while CCombat +0x1C is under NAVAL_COMBAT_SUB_SURPRISE_ROUNDS, because the function reads its own flag byte (+0x25) as the last round left it before the base clears it; a later fleet of the side shares an earlier one's success. The formulas are in reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatmods.md, section 6. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seabattle.md, section 3. **BM_LEADER_BONUS behind CUnit::LeaderHasRankForCommand inlined** - the jump table on oob_level, rank 3, 3, 2, 1, pass, then slot 15 or CLeader::CommandSize >= the regiments, pass - and skill > 0: `skill * 1000 * COMBAT_LEADER_IMPACT / 1000` on both halves, no trait. Traits by CommandEffect: 10 out_of_supply_modifier on the supply lack and 23 experience_bonus on the experience, each x (1000 + t) / 1000; 18 night_attack added to the night; none on dissent. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaairleaders.md, section 1.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x566CAC..0x566E18 with the table at 0x566E48 (0x566CC6, 0x566CDB, 0x566CF0, 0x566D05, 0x566D50, 0x566D1A, 0x566D1A, 0x566D50) against 0x5CD960's at 0x5CD9C0; the push 0xA at 0x566AEC before the CommandEffect call at 0x566AF7.
addresses.revises: Adds the inlined rank ladder and the three trait kinds, the supply one read by hand.

addresses.name: CAirCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CAirCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers(CAirCombatant* this, CCombatant* other, int flag)
addresses.comment: Slot 19 for an air fight. Not read through. **Read as far as its defines, 2026-10-05 (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airdefence.md).** Slot 19 is where everything that shapes an air fight other than `air_attack` lives, and it reads nine named `military` defines: AIR_STACKING_PENALTY (0x16C747) and AIR_STACKING_PENALTY_MAX (0x16C77B), BASE_PROXIMITY_BONUS (0x16CB70), INTERCEPT_ATTACK_BONUS (0x16CC27), AIR_SUP_DEFEND_BONUS (0x16CCD5), RADAR_COMBAT_IMPACT (0x16D080 and 0x16D34E), COMBAT_SUPPLY_LACK_IMPACT (0x16CE3A), COMBAT_DISSENT_IMPACT (0x16CFA4), PRIDE_BONUS_EXP (0x16C9F8) - and RIVER_CROSSING_PENALTY at 0x16D1DB, which in an air fight is odd enough to deserve a look. **Its four `+0x128` reads are CUnit::owner_id, not `air_defence`** (0x16C917, 0x16CD1B, 0x16CEBC, 0x16CF06): each pairs the tag letters at +0x124 with the id and indexes the country array at [0x1A855A4] +0x16C. Nothing reachable from an air combat reads `air_defence` - the closure is 529 functions and the finding has the method. **Read as far as its leader, 2026-10-11:** **BM_LEADER_BONUS behind CUnit::LeaderHasRankForCommand inlined** - the jump table on oob_level, rank 3, 3, 2, 1, pass, then slot 15 or CLeader::CommandSize >= the regiments, pass - and skill > 0: `skill * 1000 * COMBAT_LEADER_IMPACT / 1000` on both halves, no trait. Traits by CommandEffect: 10 out_of_supply_modifier on the supply lack and 23 experience_bonus on the experience, each x (1000 + t) / 1000; 18 night_attack added to the night; none on dissent. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaairleaders.md, section 1.
addresses.evidence: CLeader::CommandSize called at 0x56D2BD; CommandEffect at 0x56CA21 (push 0x17), 0x56CE48 (push 0xA at 0x56CE3D) and 0x56D1FF (push 0x12).
addresses.revises: Adds the leader's bonus and the three trait kinds to an entry that was read only as far as its defines.

addresses.name: CBomberCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers

Traits by CommandEffect: 10 out_of_supply_modifier on the supply lack and 23 experience_bonus on the experience, each x (1000 + t) / 1000; 18 night_attack added to the night; none on dissent. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaairleaders.md, section 1.

addresses.name: CNavalCombatant::AddUnit
addresses.comment: CCombatant slot 12 for a naval side: **where every ship is given its distance.** After the base (CCombatant::AddUnit) and CNavalCombatant::UpdatePositioning it counts the unit's ships by type into +0x74 and then sets each ship's current_distance (CSubUnit +0xC8): half the definition's firing_distance, plus a roll of up to `max(300 - spread_out trait, 100) / 1000 * half * (5 - leader skill) * (1 - positioning)` (2 at least); the fleet's first capital ship sets a line, every other ship is put before or behind that line at even odds; a unit joining a battle that has had a round starts 100.000 further out, measured from the side's first capital ship that has a distance; never under 1.000. The 300 is the floor of the float 300.5 (0x1A881A8). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seabattle.md, section 2. **The leader is the unit's own (+0x12C), with no rank test**, and `5 - skill` is held at nothing (0x566FEC). An admiral of skill 5 or more leaves the roll at its floor of 2, so his ships stand at half their reach **or one further** - not exactly half, as FINDINGS-seabattle.md section 2 says. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaairleaders.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: 0x566FCB mov edx,[ebx+0x12C]; 0x566FD6 sub esi,[edx+0x70]; 0x566FEC test esi,esi; jns; the floor 2000 applied after the (1000 - positioning) product. What would show it wrong: a rank test between 0x566FCB and 0x566FD6 - there is none.
addresses.revises: Adds whose leader it is and corrects 'exactly half' to half or one further.

addresses.name: CSubUnit::PickTarget
addresses.signature: CSubUnit* __thiscall CSubUnit::PickTarget(CSubUnit* attacker, CNavalCombatant* side, CCombatant* other)
addresses.comment: **Who a ship shoots at this hour.** `p = (definition.positioning + side.positioning) * 100 * (1 + the country's naval_positioning_bonus, the technology key targeting_chance)`, a whole number, halved at night for the second test. A remembered target (+0xB8/+0xBC) that still exists is forgotten on `Random() % 50 > p + 10`, and at night on a further `Random() % 100 > 80`; one of another country is kept only while its fleet is on the other side, and one of the ship's own country is kept a quarter of the time. With none: `Random() % 80 > p` means the ship has lost the enemy - no target, or with `Random() % 100 < 7 - the skill of the side's highest ranked leader` (CCombatant::GetHighestRankedLeader of its own side, where his slot 8 answers yes) **one of its own side's ships** (the walk does not stop at the ship drawn and ends on the last one of the side). Otherwise CNavalCombatant::CollectTargets fills the side's list with the enemy ships in reach, and the target is a random one of them, or - on `Random() % 100 <= CSubUnit::TargetingSkill / 10` - CNavalCombatant::PickBestTarget's. The pick is remembered. So positioning buys a ship a target at all, and keeps the one it has. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seabattle.md, section 4. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaairleaders.md, section 4.
addresses.evidence: 0x5677D3 lea esi,[ecx-0x49] with ecx 0x50; 0x5677D6 and 0x5677E9 call 0x565F20 with ebx, the function's [ebp+8], its own side; 0x5677EE sub esi,[eax+0x70].
addresses.revises: The friendly fire's leader is the side's highest ranked, not the ship's admiral; and the technology figure's key.

addresses.name: CSubUnit::TargetingSkill
addresses.comment: Ten times the skill of the sub unit's unit's own leader (+0xB0 -> +0x12C -> +0x70), with no rank test, plus a technology figure of its owner (CSubUnit::GetOwner): CTechnologyStatus +0x74 (`targeting_choice`) for a ship (slot 10); for a wing (slot 11) `bomber_targeting` (+0xC8) and `fighter_targeting` (+0xCC) **added together**, whatever the wing or its target is; a brigade, neither. The ten is the global at 0x1A8868C, floor(10.5) written at 0xCC370B; the leader's part is ten a point raw and the technology's thousandths. CSubUnit::PickTarget and CAirCombatant::PickTarget take a tenth of it as the chance in a hundred of the best target in place of a random one. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaairleaders.md, section 4.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x5AC3C0..0x5AC42E; staticconst on 0x1A8868C finds one writer, at 0xCC370B, loading 10.5.
addresses.revises: Names the static, the leader as the unit's own with no rank test, and the ship's key.

addresses.name: WantsToDisengage
addresses.comment: `limit = (1000 + *CUnit::GetTraitEffect(unit, &tmp, 0xC)) * 5000 / 1000 / 1000`, the last a divide by the magic 0x10624DD3 - so 5 x (1 + disengage_timer) **cut to a whole number toward nothing**; `return unit->disengage (+0xA8) >= limit`. Trait effect 0xC is `disengage_timer` (CTrait::Effect entry 12), so with no trait the limit is 5, and a trait of -0.1 still leaves 4. `this` in ESI, bare ret, no stack arguments. Called from CNavalCombat::Tick's disengage loop; a true answer ends the whole combat. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaairleaders.md, section 6.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x5C9A60..0x5C9AB4: __allmul by 0x1388, __alldiv by 0x3E8, then imul 0x10624DD3; sar edx,6 and the sign fix at 0x5C9A97..0x5C9AA6.
addresses.revises: Says the limit is cut to a whole number, and places the return.

addresses.name: CCombatant::CollectBombTargets
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CCombatant::CollectBombTargets(CCombatant* this, CBomberCombatant* bombers, CUnit* bomber)
addresses.comment: Makes the bombers' list out of this side's units: an air unit only under the bomber's order's slot 29 and slot 17 and only at its own base, a land unit only under slot 28, a fleet only under slot 27 or a convoy raid's order (0x592); every brigade, wing or ship with strength left, 1024 at most. **A ship, under any order but the convoy raid's, only by a roll of its own**: `Random() % 100 <= the bomber's leader's skill x 10 x (1000 + naval_air_target_chance) / 1000`, CTechnologyStatus +0xD8 - the leader read off CUnit +0x12C with no test for none, which is the empty leader. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 6. The leader is the bomber unit's own, with no rank test (0x5609CD). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaairleaders.md, section 5.
addresses.evidence: 0x5609CD mov ecx,[edi+0x12C]; 0x5609D3 mov eax,[ecx+0x70], with edi's +0x124/+0x128 the owner whose technology +0xD8 follows.
addresses.revises: Says the leader is the bomber's own and asked for no rank.

struct_fields.name: naval_positioning_bonus
struct_fields.comment: **The technology effect `targeting_chance`** (CTechStatistics::LoadKey token 0x511, reversing/findings/FINDINGS-fieldmap.md; the tooltip's TARGET_CHANCE_TECH, reversing/findings/FINDINGS-uinumbers2.md section 4). Scales a ship's positioning score in CSubUnit::PickTarget (0x16764F): `p = p * (1000 + this) / 1000`, where p is the ship definition's `positioning` plus the combatant's accumulated +0x10B4. Thousandths. The record's name is from its use and is kept. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaairleaders.md, section 4.
struct_fields.evidence: The fieldmap table places token 0x511 at +0x70; the one reader is 0x56764C. What would show it wrong: a second LoadKey arm writing +0x70.
struct_fields.revises: The comment said the name was ours; the key was in the fieldmap all along.

struct_fields.name: naval_targeting_bonus
struct_fields.comment: **The technology effect `targeting_choice`** (CTechStatistics::LoadKey token 0x510, reversing/findings/FINDINGS-fieldmap.md; the tooltip's TARGET_CHOICE_TECH, reversing/findings/FINDINGS-uinumbers2.md section 4). CSubUnit::TargetingSkill adds it for a ship: a tenth of that sum, with ten for each point of the admiral's skill, is the chance in a hundred that a ship takes the best target in reach. Thousandths. The record's name is from its use and is kept. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaairleaders.md, section 4.
struct_fields.evidence: The fieldmap table places token 0x510 at +0x74; read at 0x5AC407. What would show it wrong: a second LoadKey arm writing +0x74.
struct_fields.revises: The comment said which technology key fills it was not read; the fieldmap has it.
